title: Command-line word count
description:
Write a small `wc` that counts lines, words and bytes with only the standard library.

```
  3  12  62 notes.txt
  1   4  20 todo.txt
  4  16  82 total
```
hints: Keep `int in_word = 0;`: a word starts when you see a non-space character while `in_word` is 0 (lesson 6.04).
`int c; while ((c = fgetc(f)) != EOF)`: `c` must be an `int`, not a `char`, so `EOF` can be told apart from a real byte.
requirements: Create two files at the start, then count each one with `fgetc` in one pass.
A word is a run of characters that are not `isspace`.
Print columns with `%3d`, and a total line when there is more than one file.
Report a file that cannot be opened with `perror` and carry on.
stretch: Add `-l`, `-w` and `-c` options to print only some columns.
